title: Check yourself: virtual and platform threads

questions.stem: A Java 21 service runs on 8 carriers. Its config holder has a `synchronized` method `reload()` that, if the config has expired, fetches a fresh copy from the config server over HTTP, which takes 3 seconds. When the config expires, 30 request threads, all virtual, call `reload()` at the same moment. A health check arrives on a new virtual thread one second later. What happens to it?

options.text: It runs at once, since the 30 threads blocked on reload() all give their 8 carriers back
options.says: on Java 21 a virtual thread inside synchronized, or waiting to enter it, can't unmount: it is pinned

options.text: It runs at once, since only the thread inside reload() pins a carrier and the others park
options.says: a virtual thread waiting to enter a monitor is pinned too, so the waiting threads hold the other 7 carriers

options.text: It waits until reload() returns, since the threads waiting to enter it pin the remaining carriers
options.says: the holder pins one carrier and seven waiting threads pin the rest; nothing else runs until the reload returns

options.text: It waits until the scheduler adds a 9th carrier, which it does once all 8 carriers are pinned
options.says: the scheduler adds no carrier for a thread pinned in synchronized; the unrelated task in the unit waited for the whole refresh

origin.section: On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier

questions.stem: A batch tool's `main` creates its export thread with `Thread exporter = Thread.ofVirtual().unstarted(exportTask)`, then has the lines `exporter.setDaemon(false);` (so that the JVM waits for the file to be written) and `exporter.start();`, and then returns. What happens when the tool runs?

options.text: The export finishes before the JVM exits, since setDaemon(false) made the thread keep the JVM alive
options.says: a virtual thread is always a daemon; setDaemon(false) on one throws IllegalArgumentException

options.text: The export finishes before the JVM exits, since a thread inherits its creator's non-daemon status
options.says: that inheritance holds for platform threads; a virtual thread is a daemon whoever creates it

options.text: The setDaemon(false) call throws, so main never reaches start() and the export never runs
options.says: setDaemon(false) on a virtual thread throws IllegalArgumentException: 'false' not legal for virtual threads

options.text: The setDaemon(false) call is ignored, so the JVM can exit while the export is still writing
options.says: setPriority is the setter that is ignored; setDaemon(false) throws before start() is reached

origin.section: A Virtual Thread Is Always a Daemon, at Normal Priority

questions.stem: A Java 21 service stalls for 2 seconds at a time. Its `synchronized` method `refresh()` calls a pricing API that takes 2 seconds, and during a stall one virtual thread is inside `refresh()` while seven more are waiting to enter it. The team restarts the service with `-Djdk.tracePinnedThreads=short` and watches the next stall. What does the property print?

options.text: Eight stacks, one per thread pinned by refresh(), since waiting to enter it also pins a carrier
options.says: waiting to enter a monitor does pin on Java 21, but the property names the holder only; the threads waiting to enter don't appear

options.text: Seven stacks, those of the threads waiting to enter, since only they are blocked on the monitor
options.says: the property prints the stack where a pinned virtual thread blocked: the holder's, inside refresh(), marked reason:MONITOR; the threads waiting to enter don't appear

options.text: One stack, that of the thread inside refresh(), since it blocked while holding the monitor
options.says: on Java 21 the property prints the stack where a pinned virtual thread blocked, marked reason:MONITOR, and it names the holder only

options.text: No stacks, since the property was removed and only a JFR recording reports pinning now
options.says: the property was removed in Java 24 and later; on Java 21 it prints the stack where a pinned virtual thread blocked

origin.section: On Java 21, Blocking Inside synchronized Holds the Carrier
